notes: KNOWN FAILING — GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 genuinely supports agent-driven background processes. The account's live `bash` tool input_schema (captured in ~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log) carries a `detach` boolean whose own description reads "Without `detach`, a command remains attached and keeps running after `initial_wait` and across turns until it completes, is stopped, or the CLI exits", with `read_bash` / `stop_bash` / `list_bash` companions — the direct analogue of Claude Code's run_in_background + BashOutput + KillShell. But the copilot adapter (core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/parser.go) has NO background-process tracking: it sets none of ParsedEvent.BackgroundSpawns / BashOutputPolls / TerminatedBashOutputIDs / KilledShellIDs and handles no `system.notification` envelope, so BackgroundProcessCount stays 0 and the session settles to ready on assistant.turn_end while the detached process is still alive. RECIPE: the prompt starts `sleep 45 && echo BG_DONE` with detach:true, calls list_bash once (so the shell's PID lands in the transcript — the probe anchor any fix will need), and replies done IMMEDIATELY without polling, so the turn ends well before the 45s process does. CORRECT arc: ready→working, working HELD until the detached process exits (~45s), then a single working→ready. bg_alive_working asserts working persists for 30000ms (longer than the ~15s turn, shorter than the 45s bg lifetime) — the daemon settles to ready at turn-end instead, so this phase is EXPECTED to fail. Fix is the Copilot parallel of #450/#445 in the copilot parser (spawn from tool.execution_complete.data.toolTelemetry.properties.detached=="true" plus the `<command started in detached background with shellId: …>` result text; close on the persisted system.notification whose kind.type is shell_detached_completed) AND a liveness anchor for SessionDetector.hasBackgroundProbe (a PID from list_bash, or the runtime's shell-logs/ output file); re-record and clear known_failing then. OBSERVATIONS: cost/tokens asserted non-zero only; `model` is deliberately unpinned — --model accepts only 'auto' on this account and the router picks per turn between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5. PRESESSION BIRTH: copilot creates its session-state directory at launch but writes events.jsonl only at the first prompt, so a transient proc-<PID> row appears first and the real dir-keyed session id arrives later — modelled as two phases with every later phase anchored same_session_as session_birth.
